prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1328; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle was struck from behind by Driver 2's sedan. Officers arrived to find both vehicles stopped on the shoulder. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy and was present at the scene. Passenger was seated in the front passenger position and was in the vehicle at the time of impact, a fact confirmed by both drivers and by two independent witnesses who had been stopped behind the vehicles. Passenger reported wrist pain and was transported for evaluation, where a wrist fracture was noted. The rear bumper and trunk area of Driver 1's vehicle show damage consistent with the reported impact, and officers photographed the scene and the damage. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was known to Driver 1, Driver 2, or the witnesses. Driver 2 confirmed the sequence of events as described by Driver 1 and the witnesses. The force of the collision appears consistent with the injury Passenger reported.
